cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For patients with normal renal function (eGFR >=90), the starting dose of AX-17 is 50 mg OD, with a maximum dose of 100 mg/day and routine monitoring [E2]. For mild renal impairment (eGFR 60-89), the starting dose is also 50 mg OD, with a maximum of 100 mg/day and routine monitoring [E2].

For moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the approved German renal starting dose is 25 mg once daily [E1, E3], with a maximum dose of 50 mg/day and monitoring involving a recheck in 2-4 weeks [E2].

For severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29), a specialist review is required for the starting dose, the maximum dose is 25 mg/day, and enhanced monitoring is needed [E2].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
AX-17 requires temporary hepatic monitoring enhancement, where baseline hepatic laboratory values are required with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. If ALT/AST is >3x ULN, medical review is required [E2]. If Bilirubin is >2x ULN, urgent review is required [E2]. If there is a mild isolated change below trigger, a repeat test is required [E2]. The approved German renal starting dose is 25 mg once daily for moderate renal impairment [E1].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
Both HN-204 and HN-311 reported treatment-emergent adverse events including nausea, headache, fatigue, dizziness, rash, and transaminase elevation [E1, E2, E3]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in both studies, while nausea, headache, fatigue, dizziness, and rash were not serious [E1, E2].

In HN-204, the percentages for AX-17 and Control were:
*   Nausea: 12.7% (AX-17), 6.0% (Control) [E1, E3]
*   Headache: 14.0% (AX-17), 6.6% (Control) [E1, E3]
*   Fatigue: 15.3% (AX-17), 7.2% (Control) [E1, E3]
*   Dizziness: 16.6% (AX-17), 7.8% (Control) [E1, E3]
*   Rash: 17.8% (AX-17), 8.4% (Control) [E1, E3]
*   Transaminase elevation: 19.1% (AX-17), 9.0% (Control) [E1, E3]

In HN-311, the percentages for AX-17 and Control were:
*   Nausea: 11.8% (AX-17), 6.0% (Control) [E2, E3]
*   Headache: 13.0% (AX-17), 6.6% (Control) [E2, E3]
*   Fatigue: 14.2% (AX-17), 7.2% (Control) [E2, E3]
*   Dizziness: 15.4% (AX-17), 7.8% (Control) [E2, E3]
*   Rash: 16.6% (AX-17), 8.4% (Control) [E2, E3]
*   Transaminase elevation: 17.7% (AX-17), 9.0% (Control) [E2, E3]

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the treatment % for AX-17 was lower in HN-311 for all listed events, with differences ranging from -0.9 to -1.4 points [E4]. Specifically:
*   Nausea: -0.9 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]
*   Headache: -1.0 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]
*   Fatigue: -1.1 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]
*   Dizziness: -1.2 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]
*   Rash: -1.2 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]
*   Transaminase elevation: -1.4 points (HN-311 minus HN-204) [E4]

For control groups, the percentages were identical across both studies for all listed events [E3, E4].

In both HN-204 and HN-311, the highest treatment % for AX-17 was transaminase elevation, at 19.1% in HN-204 and 17.7% in HN-311 [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14

[E3] v_adverse_events (registry database, verified read-only query) · rows for HN-204, HN-311
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

cases.question: What hepatic monitoring is required for AX-17 in Germany?
cases.answer:
For AX-17 in Germany, baseline hepatic laboratory values are required [E1]. Repeat testing is needed between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. Specific actions are mandated based on thresholds: if ALT/AST is >3x ULN, a Medical review is required [E2]; if Bilirubin is >2x ULN, an Urgent review is required [E2]; and for a mild isolated change below the trigger, a Repeat test is required [E2].
